source.title: Open problems in commutative ring theory

accepted.question_text: Let R be a Prüfer ring, meaning that every finitely generated regular ideal of R is invertible. Is the finitistic projective dimension fp.dim R at most 1?

evidence.quote: Problem 1a. Let R be a Prüfer ring. Is fp.dim R ≤ 1?

accepted.question_text: Let R be a total ring of quotients. Must its finitistic projective dimension satisfy fp.dim R = 0? Since every total ring of quotients is a Prüfer ring, this asks whether this special class always has finitistic projective dimension exactly zero, not just at most one.
accepted.context_brief: Total quotient rings and finitistic dimension

evidence.quote: Problem 1b. Let R be a total ring of quotients. Is fp.dim R = 0?

accepted.question_text: If R is a Gaussian ring, meaning that c(fg) = c(f)c(g) for all polynomials f,g in R[x], must the weak global dimension w.dim R always be one of the values 0, 1, or infinity?

evidence.quote: Problem 2a. If R is a Gaussian ring, then is w.dim R = 0; 1, or ∞?

accepted.question_text: If R is a total ring of quotients, must the weak global dimension w.dim R always be one of the values 0, 1, or infinity?
accepted.context_brief: Total quotient rings and weak dimension

evidence.quote: Problem 2b. If R is a total ring of quotients, is w.dim R = 0; 1, or ∞?

accepted.question_text: What values can the weak global dimension w.dim R take when R is a Prüfer ring?

evidence.quote: Problem 2c. What are the values of w.dim R when R is a Prüfer ring?

accepted.question_text: If D is a one-dimensional coherent domain, is the integral closure of D in its field of quotients necessarily a Prüfer domain?

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Is the integral closure of a one dimensional coherent domain in its field of quotients a Prüfer domain?

accepted.question_text: Assume R is a G-GCD ring and G is a finitely generated abelian group. Do the finite conductor property and the quasi coherent property always ascend from R to the group ring RG?

evidence.quote: Problem 4a. Assume that R is a G-GCD ring and G is a finitely generated abelian group. Do the finite conductor and the quasi coherent properties ascend from R to RG?

accepted.question_text: Are the finite conductor property and the quasi coherent property genuinely different properties for commutative rings, or do they coincide?
accepted.context_brief: Finite conductor versus quasi coherent rings

evidence.quote: Problem 4b. Are the finite conductor and quasi coherent properties for rings distinct?

accepted.question_text: For a commutative ring R and an abelian group G such that the order of every element of G is invertible in R, is there a formula expressing the global dimension of the group ring RG in terms of the global dimension of R together with some invariant of G, analogous to the known weak-dimension formula w.dim RG = w.dim R + rank G?

evidence.quote: Problem 5a. Is there a similar formula that relates the global dimension of RG to the global dimension of R in combination with some invariant of the group G?

accepted.question_text: Find characterizations of commutative group rings that are semisimple and of those that are hereditary; equivalently, characterize when a group ring has global dimension 0 or 1 in these cases.

evidence.quote: Problem 5b. Find characterizations of semisimple and hereditary group rings.

accepted.question_text: Determine when a commutative group ring RG, where R is a commutative ring and G is an abelian group, is Cohen-Macaulay or Gorenstein in the non-Noetherian sense developed in the cited literature.
accepted.context_brief: Non-Noetherian Cohen-Macaulay and Gorenstein group rings

evidence.quote: the questions of when a group ring RG, where R is a commutative ring and G is an abelian group, is Cohen-Macaulay or Gorenstein have yet to be investigated.

accepted.question_text: Develop a non-Noetherian characterization of local complete intersection rings that is compatible with the coherent local theories in the sense that coherent local Gorenstein rings are complete intersections and coherent local complete intersection rings are Cohen-Macaulay.

evidence.quote: Is there a non-Noetherian characterization of local complete intersection rings such that (coherent) local Gorenstein rings are complete intersections, and such that (coherent) local complete intersection rings are Cohen-Macaulay?

accepted.question_text: If a Noetherian local ring is weakly quasi-complete, must it already be quasi-complete?

evidence.quote: Problem 8a. Is a weakly quasi-complete ring quasi-complete?

accepted.question_text: Let k be a field and let R = k[X1, ..., Xn]_(X1,...,Xn) with n at least 2. Is R weakly quasi-complete, or equivalently quasi-complete?

evidence.quote: Problem 8b. Let k be a field and R = k[X1; : : : ; Xn]_(X1,...,Xn), n ≥ 2. Is R (weakly) quasi-complete?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an integrally closed reduced ring R such that for every maximal ideal M the localization R_M is an integrally closed McCoy ring, while R itself is not a McCoy ring and is not locally a domain?

evidence.quote: Does there exist an integrally closed reduced ring R such that RM is an integrally closed McCoy ring for each maximal ideal M, but R is not a McCoy ring and it is not locally a domain?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist reduced rings that satisfy both the annihilator condition (a.c.) and property (A_n) for some n at least 2, but are nevertheless not McCoy rings?

evidence.quote: Do there exist reduced rings that have both (a.c.) and (A_n) for some n ≥ 2 that are not McCoy rings?

accepted.question_text: Let R be a Prüfer domain and P a nonzero prime ideal of R. Characterize those pairs (P,R) such that for every Prüfer domain T contained in R with the same quotient field, the contraction P ∩ T is a divisorial prime ideal of T.

evidence.quote: Problem 11a. Characterize when P (and R) is such that P∩T is a divisorial prime of T for each Prüfer domain T ⊆ R with the same quotient field as R.

accepted.question_text: Let R be a Prüfer domain and P a nonzero prime ideal of R. Characterize those pairs (P,R) for which there is no Prüfer domain T contained in R with the same quotient field such that P ∩ T is a divisorial prime ideal of T.

evidence.quote: Problem 11b. Characterize when P (and R) is such that there is no Prüfer domain T ⊆ R with the same quotient field as R such that P ∩ T is a divisorial prime of T.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Prüfer domain R with a nonzero prime ideal P and a countably infinite chain of overrings R = R0 ⊊ R1 ⊊ R2 ⊊ ··· ⊊ R_P such that for every n at least 0, the extended ideal P R_{2n} is divisorial in R_{2n} while P R_{2n+1} is not divisorial in R_{2n+1}? If such a chain exists, is P S divisorial or not in the union S = ⋃ R_m?

evidence.quote: Problem 12a. Does there exist a Prüfer domain R with a nonzero prime P such that there is a countably infinite chain of overrings R = R0 ⊊ R1 ⊊ R2 ⊊ ··· ⊊ RP where for all n ≥ 0, PR2n is a divisorial ideal of R2n and PR2n+1 is an ideal of R2n+1 that is not divisorial? If such a chain exists, is PS divisorial or not divisorial as an ideal of S = ⋃Rm (⊆ RP)?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Prüfer domain R with a nonzero prime ideal P and a countably infinite chain of underrings R = R0 ⊋ R1 ⊋ R2 ⊋ ··· ⊋ T = ⋂ R_m, where T has the same quotient field as R, such that for every n at least 0 the contracted ideal P ∩ R_{2n} is divisorial in R_{2n} while P ∩ R_{2n+1} is not divisorial in R_{2n+1}? If such a chain exists, is P ∩ T divisorial or not in T?

evidence.quote: Problem 12b. Does there exist a Prüfer domain R with a nonzero prime P such that there is a countably infinite chain of underrings R = R0 ⊋ R1 ⊋ R2 ⊋ ··· ⊋ T = ⋂Rm with T having the same quotient field as R where for all n ≥ 0, P ∩ R2n is a divisorial ideal of R2n and P ∩ R2n+1 is not a divisorial ideal of R2n+1? If such a chain exists, is P ∩ T divisorial or not divisorial as an ideal of T?

accepted.question_text: If R_P and R/P are straight domains, does it follow that the pullback-type domain R + P R_P is also a straight domain?

evidence.quote: Problem 13a. If RP and R/P are straight domains does this imply that R + PRP is a straight domain?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a straight domain that is not locally divided?

evidence.quote: Problem 13b. Does there exist a straight domain which is not locally divided?

accepted.question_text: For an integral domain D, is the Krull dimension of the ring Int(D) of integer-valued polynomials always at most the Krull dimension of the ordinary polynomial ring D[X]? Equivalently, does dim(Int(D)) ≤ dim(D[X]) always hold?

evidence.quote: The question of an upper bound remains open: It is conjectured to be equal to dim(D[X]).

accepted.question_text: Let D be a one-dimensional local Noetherian domain with finite residue field. Find a necessary and sufficient condition for the integer-valued polynomial ring Int(D) to satisfy the almost strong Skolem property.

evidence.quote: Problem 15. Considering a one-dimensional local Noetherian domain D with finite residue field, when does Int(D) satisfy the almost strong Skolem property?

accepted.question_text: Are there natural self-ordered sequences of integers other than those obtained from the known dynamical constructions and their affine transforms, and other than the three listed candidate examples discussed in the source?

evidence.quote: Are there any other ‘natural’ self ordered sequences neither obtained by a dynamical construction nor by an affine map applied to the three previous examples?

accepted.question_text: Do there exist subsets E of the integers such that the associated sequence of Bhargava factorials (n!_E) is not ultimately strictly increasing?

evidence.quote: Are there subsets E of Z such that the sequence of Bhargava’s factorials {n!E} is not ultimately strictly increasing?

accepted.question_text: For which infinite subsets E of the integers is the generalized constant e_E associated to the Bhargava factorials of E a transcendental number?

evidence.quote: For which infinite subset E is eE a transcendental number?

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary integral domain D, is Int(D) always a flat D-module?

evidence.quote: Problem 19a. Is Int(D) a flat D module for any domain D?

accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary integral domain D, is Int(D) always a free D-module?

evidence.quote: Problem 19b. Is Int(D) a free D-module for any domain D?

accepted.question_text: Let D be an integral domain. Is the canonical D-algebra homomorphism Int(D)^⊗n → Int(D^n) always injective, always surjective, or both?

evidence.quote: Is this canonical morphism always injective? surjective?

accepted.question_text: Let D be an integral domain. Does Int(D) always admit a unique structure of a D-D-biring such that the inclusion D[X] → Int(D) is a homomorphism of D-D-birings?

evidence.quote: Let D be an integral domain. Does Int(D) always have a unique structure of a D-D-biring such that the inclusion D[X] → Int(D) is a homomorphism of D-D-birings?

accepted.question_text: If D ⊆ A is an extension of domains and Int(D) ⊆ Int(A), must the extension D ⊆ A be almost polynomially complete, meaning that Int(D^n) ⊆ Int(A^n) for all positive integers n?

evidence.quote: If Int(D) ⊆ Int(A), does it follow that the extension D ⊆ A is almost polynomially complete?

accepted.question_text: Let K be a number field with ring of integers O_K, and let δ(Int(O_K)) denote the natural density of nonnegative integers n for which the O_K-module Int_n(O_K) is free. Does this density always exist, is it always rational, is it always at least 1 / Card(PO(O_K)), and can one compute it explicitly?
accepted.context_brief: Density of free truncations of Int(O_K)

evidence.quote: Prove or disprove the following conjecture [38]: δ(Int(OK)) exists, is rational, and is at least 1/Card(PO(OK)) ... Then compute δ(Int(OK)).

accepted.question_text: Let E be the set of values of a second-order recursive integer sequence u_{n+1} = a u_n + b u_{n-1} with given initial values u_0 and u_1. Compute a regular basis of the Z-module Int(E,Z), compute its characteristic sequence with respect to each prime p, and determine the asymptotic behavior of that characteristic sequence.

evidence.quote: Problem 24a. Compute a regular basis ... Problem 24b. Compute the characteristic sequence ... Problem 24c. Determine the asymptotic behavior of this sequence

accepted.question_text: For the ring Int_Q(M_n(Z)) of rational polynomials that are integer-valued on n × n integer matrices, compute a regular basis, compute the characteristic sequence with respect to each prime p, and determine the asymptotic behavior of that sequence.

evidence.quote: Problem 25a. Compute a regular basis of IntQ(Mn(Z)). Problem 25b. Compute its characteristic sequence with respect to each prime p. Problem 25c. Determine the asymptotic behavior of this sequence.

accepted.question_text: Let D be an integral domain, K its quotient field, and A a torsion-free D-algebra that is finitely generated as a D-module. Characterize those algebras A for which the inclusion ⋂_{a in A}(D[X] + μ_a(X)K[X]) ⊆ Int_K(A) is actually an equality.

evidence.quote: For which algebras A as above does this inclusion become an equality?

accepted.question_text: Give an example of a D-algebra A, possibly after relaxing some of the standing hypotheses such as finite generation as a D-module, for which the set Int(A) of polynomials over the total quotient algebra that are integer-valued on A is not a ring. Also determine whether the conjecture that Int(A) is always a ring when D has finite residue rings is true or false.
accepted.context_brief: Ring structure of Int(A) for noncommutative algebras

evidence.quote: Problem 27a. Give an example of a D-algebra A such that Int(A) is not a ring ... Problem 27b. ... it is conjectured that Int(A) is always a ring when D has finite residue rings. Prove this conjecture or give a counterexample in this case.

accepted.question_text: Let D be an integral domain with quotient field K and A a D-algebra. Determine when the integral closure of Int_K(A) is a Prüfer domain.
accepted.context_brief: Prüfer property for integral closures of Int_K(A)

evidence.quote: Determine when this integral closure is Prüfer.

accepted.question_text: Describe the integrally closed rings lying between a two-dimensional Noetherian domain and its quotient field.

evidence.quote: Describe the integrally closed rings between a two-dimensional Noetherian domain and its quotient field.

accepted.question_text: Let R be a ring and n a positive integer. If I is an n-absorbing ideal of R, must I be strongly n-absorbing? Must rad(I)^n be contained in I? And must I[X] be an n-absorbing ideal of the polynomial ring R[X]?

evidence.quote: Problem 30a. Let I be an n-absorbing ideal of R. Is I a strongly n-absorbing ideal of R? ... Problem 30b. Let I be an n-absorbing ideal of R. Is rad(I)^n ⊆ I?
Problem 30c. Let I be an n-absorbing ideal of R. Is I[X] an n-absorbing ideal of the polynomial ring R[X]?

accepted.question_text: Develop a theory of projective star operations for projective varieties, equivalently for finitely generated field extensions F/K that need not be purely transcendental, extending the existing theory built for projective n-space.

evidence.quote: Develop projective star operations for projective varieties (i.e., for the case where F/K is a finitely generated field extension that need not be purely transcendental)?

accepted.question_text: Is every stable Archimedean domain one-dimensional? If D is a one-dimensional Mori domain in which each divisorial ideal is 2-v-generated, must every divisorial ideal be stable? More generally, if D is a Mori domain in which each divisorial ideal is 2-v-generated, must D be v-stable?

evidence.quote: Problem 32a. Is a stable Archimedean domain one-dimensional?

Problem 32b. Let D be a one-dimensional Mori domain such that each divisorial ideal is 2-v-generated. Is it true that each divisorial ideal is stable? ... Problem 32c. Let D be a Mori domain such that each divisorial ideal is 2-v-generated. Is it true that D is v-stable?

accepted.question_text: Assume that D is a finitely stable LPI-domain. Must D have finite character?
accepted.context_brief: Finite character of finitely stable LPI-domains

evidence.quote: Assume that D is a finitely stable LPI-domain. Is it true that D has finite character?

accepted.question_text: Find necessary and sufficient conditions for the ring R = D + X D_S[X] to be a v-domain, and determine whether R is a v-domain exactly when D is a v-domain and each ideal (d, X) is v-invertible for every nonzero d in D. More generally, for an extension of integral domains A ⊆ B, find necessary and sufficient conditions for A + X B[X] to be a v-domain.
accepted.context_brief: v-domains of D + X D_S[X] type

evidence.quote: Problem 34a. Find necessary and sufficient conditions for R = D + XDS[X] to be a v-domain. Prove or disprove that R is a v-domain if and only if D is a v-domain and (d; X) is v-invertible for all d ∈ D\{0}. More generally: Problem 34b. Let A ⊆ B be an extension of integral domains ... Find necessary and sufficient conditions for the integral domain A + XB[X] to be a v-domain.

accepted.question_text: Let D be an almost GCD domain such that every nonzero t-locally principal ideal is t-invertible. Must D be of finite t-character?

evidence.quote: Let D be an almost GCD domain such that every nonzero t-locally principal ideal is t-invertible. Is D of finite t-character?

accepted.question_text: Find conditions on a family 𝒯 of overrings and semistar operations {*_T} under which the induced semistar operation *_𝒯 on D is of finite type. Equivalently, find conditions on a family 𝒮 of semistar operations such that the intersection semistar operation ˆ𝒮 is of finite type.

evidence.quote: Problem 36a. Find conditions on T and on the semistar operations ?T under which the semistar operation ?T on D ... is of finite type.
Problem 36b. ... Find conditions on the set S for the semistar operation ^S on D to be of finite type.

accepted.question_text: Is there a Krull domain, or even a factorial domain, D such that 1 + dim(D) is strictly less than dim(D[X])? Is David’s domain J locally Jaffard? More generally, if A ⊆ D is an extension of integral domains with A Noetherian and D a subalgebra of an affine domain over A, must D be locally Jaffard?

evidence.quote: Problem 37a. Is there a Krull (or, more particularly, factorial) domain D such that 1 + dim(D) < dim(D[X])?
Problem 37b. Is J a locally Jaffard domain?
Problem 37c. Let A ⊆ D be an extension of integral domains, where A is Noetherian domain and D is a subalgebra of an affine domain T over A. Is D a locally Jaffard domain?

accepted.question_text: If R is a one-dimensional local Mori domain, is R necessarily locally tame?

evidence.quote: Let R be a one-dimensional local Mori domain. Is R locally tame?

accepted.question_text: Analyze and describe non-unique factorization in Int(D) when D is a discrete valuation ring with finite residue field.

evidence.quote: Analyze and describe non-unique factorization in Int(D), where D is a DVR with finite residue field.

accepted.question_text: Find axioms characterizing the poset Spec(Q[x,y]). Determine whether Spec(Q[x,y]) and Spec(Q(√2)[x,y]) are order-isomorphic. More generally, for algebraic number fields F and K and a two-dimensional affine F-domain A, decide whether Spec(A) must be order-isomorphic to Spec(K[x,y]). Finally, if F and K are fields neither algebraic over a finite field and Spec(F[x,y]) and Spec(K[x,y]) are order-isomorphic, must F and K already be isomorphic fields?
accepted.context_brief: Order types of spectra of polynomial rings

evidence.quote: Problem 40a. Find axioms characterizing the poset Q[x; y].
Problem 40b. Are Spec(Q[x; y]) and Spec(Q(√2)[x; y]) order-isomorphic?
Problem 40c. More generally ... is Spec(A) order-isomorphic to Spec(K[x; y])?
Problem 40d. ... if Spec(F[x; y]) and Spec(K[x; y]) are order-isomorphic, are F and K necessarily isomorphic fields?

accepted.question_text: Let I be the integral closure of the ideal (x^a, y^b, z^c) in a polynomial ring in variables x, y, z over a field. Classify all triples (a,b,c) such that every power of I is integrally closed.

evidence.quote: Classify all triples (a; b; c) for which all powers of I are integrally closed.

accepted.question_text: Is there a more direct algorithm for computing the integral closure of a general ideal? In particular, can the Leonard–Pellikaan and Singh–Swanson algorithms be modified to compute integral closures of ideals?
accepted.context_brief: Algorithms for integral closure of ideals

evidence.quote: Problem 42a. Is there a more direct algorithm for computing the integral closure of a general ideal?
Problem 42b. In particular, can the Leonard–Pelikaan and Singh–Swanson algorithms be modified for computing the integral closure of ideals?

accepted.question_text: How tight is the general Lipman–Sathaye theorem stated in the source? Relax some of its assumptions and either prove that the theorem still holds or produce a counterexample for the relaxed version.

evidence.quote: The suggested problem is to find how tight is the statement of this theorem: relax some assumption and either prove the theorem or find a counterexample for that relaxation.

accepted.question_text: Construct a Noetherian, two-dimensional, complete, integrally closed local domain (R,m) in which every m-primary ideal has more than one Rees valuation, as in Cutkosky’s existence result.
accepted.context_brief: Construction of rings with multiple Rees valuations

evidence.quote: Cutkosky proved ... the existence of a Noetherian, two-dimensional, complete, integrally closed local domain (R; m) in which every m-primary ideal has more than one Rees valuation. Give a construction of such a ring.

trace.notes: Mapped the PDF as a 25-page article with one main open-problems section containing Problems 1 through 44 on pages 2-20.
Extracted explicit numbered problem statements and closely adjacent explanatory text from pages 3 through 20.

Rewrote each problem into standalone English while preserving the mathematical content supported by the cited page quotes. Closely related subparts were merged only when the source presented them as one numbered problem with lettered subquestions.
All accepted items retain page-cited verbatim evidence and were checked for self-containedness and unsupported added claims.
